question: A 53-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician in order to discuss the results of a biopsy. Two weeks ago, her mammogram revealed the presence of suspicious calcifications in her right breast, and she subsequently underwent biopsy of these lesions. Histology of the lesions revealed poorly cohesive cells growing in sheets with a nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio of 1:1. Furthermore, these cells were found to undergo invasion into the surrounding tissues. Given these findings, the patient is referred to an oncologist for further evaluation. Upon further imaging, the patient is found to have no lymph node adenopathy and no distant site metastases. Which of the following would most properly describe the lesions found in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Poorly cohesive cells growing in sheets with a nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio of 1:1 -> Invasion into surrounding tissues -> High grade -> High stage -> 80%

CHAIN: Presence of suspicious calcifications in the right breast -> Biopsy revealing poorly cohesive cells growing in sheets with a nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio of 1:1 -> Invasion into surrounding tissues -> High grade -> High stage -> 75%
enhanced_information: The lesions found in the patient are best described as high grade and high stage based on the presence of poorly cohesive cells growing in sheets with invasion into surrounding tissues. The evidence paths provided do not offer relevant support for the question at hand.
analysis: The histological features described, including poorly cohesive cells growing in sheets with invasion into surrounding tissues, are indicative of high-grade malignancy. The absence of lymph node involvement and distant metastases suggests a lower stage. Therefore, the most appropriate description for the lesions found in this patient would be high grade and low stage.
